title: The Pleasant History of the Cock and the Fox

keywords: the pleasant history of the cock and the fox
full_text:
A clever and experienced rooster named Abu Nabhan perched securely on the high branch of an ancient sycamore tree on the edge of an orchard.
A sly, hungry fox crept up to the foot of the tree, looked up, and spoke with smooth, oily sweetness:

'Peace be upon thee, noble Abu Nabhan! Hast thou heard the magnificent news proclaimed by the King of the Forest today?'
The rooster cocked his comb and looked down cautiously: 'What news, brother fox?'

The fox smiled with glistening teeth:
'A universal peace has been decreed throughout the earth! The wolf and the lamb now walk together; the hawk shares his nest with the dove; and foxes have sworn eternal brotherhood with all fowls! Come down from thy high branch, my dear brother, that we may embrace and celebrate this glorious dawn of friendship!'

Abu Nabhan, who knew the fox's treacherous nature of old, stretched his neck, stood on tiptoe, and peered intently toward the distant horizon.
'What art thou looking at so earnestly?' asked the fox, feeling uneasy.

Abu Nabhan replied with cheerful enthusiasm:
'Ah! A glorious sight! A pack of four swift greyhounds is galloping toward our tree as fast as the wind! They, too, must have heard the decree of universal peace, and are racing here to embrace us and join our festival!'

The fox's ears flattened in terror. He gathered his tail between his legs and turned to bolt into the thickets!
'Wait!' called the rooster from the branch. 'Why dost thou run away, friend fox, if the universal peace has been declared? Surely the hounds will only embrace thee!'

The fox shouted back over his shoulder as he dashed into the brush:
'Alas! What if those stupid hounds have not yet read the proclamation?'

Abu Nabhan crowed a joyful, triumphant song from his sycamore branch, laughing at how easily a predator's false flattery is scattered by a single grain of alert wit.
moral: Flattery is the trap of predators; vigilance and calm wit turn the tables on deceit.
